title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the Galois action on Teichmüller groups. This page is a hand sketch, without prose, of the simplest non-trivial symmetric cover of the projective line minus three points.

(1) Upper sphere. The six marked points 0 and ∞ (poles) and 1, i, -1, -i (equator) are the vertices of the regular octahedron on P^1(C). Small oriented loops are drawn around each point, joined to the poles by oriented meridians. These are standard generating loops of π1 of P^1 minus the six points.

(2) The Klein four-group. The maps z → -z and z → 1/z generate V = {z, -z, 1/z, -1/z}, isomorphic to F_2^2. Its non-trivial elements fix the pairs {0,∞}, {1,-1} and {i,-i}. A third written generator was crossed out.
- The quotient map is z → w = z^2 + z^{-2}. It is a Galois cover P^1 → P^1 with group V.
- It is ramified with index 2 over w = ∞, 2, -2. Riemann–Hurwitz checks: -2 = 4(-2) + 3·2.
- So P^1 minus the six octahedral points is a V-Galois étale cover of P^1 minus three points (a genus-0 dessin d'enfant).

(3) The exact sequence 1 → F_2^2 → A_4 → Z/3 → 1. This is the tetrahedral group in PGL_2 containing V as a normal subgroup. An order-3 element is, for example, z → i(z+1)/(z-1), which cycles 1→∞→i→1 and -1→0→-i→-1, i.e. it permutes the three fixed-point pairs. Hence A_4 acts on the cover. The sequence splits.

(4) Lower sphere. Now only 0, ∞, 1, -1 are punctured, with ±i marked. The relation l_∞ l_1 l_0 l_{-1} = 1 is the standard presentation of π1(P^1 - {0, ∞, 1, -1}).
- A base path β (a meridian/arc between the poles) is drawn.
- Its lifts, 'β relevé', are drawn on the other meridians. One is annotated as symmetric to another.
- This is consistent with lifting paths along the degree-2 cover z → z^2 (or the V-quotient) from P^1 - {0,1,∞} upstairs. Whether β runs along the real or the imaginary meridians is not legible.
- Purpose: to express the images of generators and of the tangential base path under such a cover. This lets one transport the Galois/GT action on π1 of P^1 minus three points to π1 of P^1 minus four points.
- This is the standard technique behind deriving relations for the Galois (later Grothendieck–Teichmüller) action from symmetric covers.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The sequence 1→F_2^2→A_4→Z/3→1 is correct (and split).
The relation l_∞ l_1 l_0 l_{-1}=1 is correct for a suitable ordering and orientation of loops.
The page gives no computation, so correctness of the intended lift formulas cannot be checked.

ideas.what: V4 = {±z, ±1/z} acting on P^1 with quotient z → z^2+z^{-2}; P^1 minus the octahedral vertices as a Galois cover of P^1 minus 3 points
ideas.modern_name: Klein four-group Galois Belyi cover / regular dessin (octahedral points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein); in the dessin context Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular polyhedra as dessins in general terms

ideas.what: Tetrahedral group as an extension of Z/3 by V4 acting on the cover
ideas.modern_name: A_4 = V_4 ⋊ Z/3 (tetrahedral subgroup of PGL_2)

ideas.what: Presentation of π1(P^1 - {0,∞,1,-1}) and lifting of a base path β along a symmetric cover to relate fundamental groups
ideas.modern_name: Use of covers M_{0,4}-type → P^1-{0,1,∞} to derive GT/Galois relations
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse d'un programme §2–3 (Teichmüller tower, two-level relations); no explicit computation published

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary sketches of a classical symmetric cover (V4 inside A_4 acting on the octahedral points) and of path-lifting for π1 of P^1 minus four points. They are useful working notes, but the content is standard and later appears systematically in the GT literature.
transcription_corrections: On the upper sphere the right-hand equatorial label reads '-1' (written like '-1'/'1') and the rear one is probably '-i'; the front centre label is 'i'.
The struck third line under 'z → 1/z' is an abandoned formula, not '-z'; it is illegible.
Lower sphere annotations read '← β relevé' (twice) and 'β relevé' (twice), plus 'β relevé, symétrique de …' (last word illegible). The plain 'β' labels sit on the central meridians.
The quotient in the exact sequence is written Z/3Z.
